# YM09: 杏花春馆 Xinghua Chunguan, "The Springtime Lodge of Apricot Blossoms"

Malone calls it The Village of Apricot Blossoms.

Wave 1 · Yuanming Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=YM09` · Page: `/scenes/#YM09` · Row: `research/buildings/YM09-xinghua-chunguan/`

## What it was

杏花春馆 Xinghua Chunguan, "Spring Lodge of Apricot Blossom", on the island south-west of 上下天光, reached across a bridge (S05 j81:1a; E1296). First a vegetable plot with a plaque of 1727; 春雨轩 was added in 1755 (S361 v2 p.25; E1303; S360 p.147, Qianlong's poem on its completion "别殿落成歌", E1287). The island holds the highest hill of the main garden but for the rock hill in the north-west, crowned by the small gate 屏岩, with the hexagonal pavilion 绿云酣 half way up (S02 p.80; E1301; S41; E1308). The main earth-god shrine of the garden stood south-west of it, facing east (S47; E1302). The editors say 春雨轩 and others outlived 1860 and were lost around 1900 (E1303); offerings were still made at the shrine in 1861 (S47 p.126; E1315). 屏岩 and 绿云酣 were excavated in 2020 (S41; E1308).

From the inventory row: **built** 康熙年间 初名菜圃 (S42); Kangxi, as the 菜圃; **changed** 1755 春雨轩 and 涧壑余清 built over the vegetable beds (S41); Malone p.80 n.: official map shows a lake and more buildings.; **destroyed** 1860; 杏花春馆 and 春雨轩 on the 1873 survival list (S06) (S05, S02, S08, S41, S42, S01, S340).

## The scene itself

### The leaf of 1744, its poem and preface

Leaf 9 of the 1744 album. Qianlong's preface: "矮屋疎籬東西參錯環植文杏春深花發爛然如霞" (low cottages and sparse fences scattered east and west, ringed with apricot trees that in late spring blaze like rosy cloud). A small plot of mixed vegetables in front gives the look of a farm village; the poem ends on spring rain and the plough (S40, printed in S05 j81:1b-2a; E1285).

### How later sources differ

By the 1780s the group was 杏花春馆 with 春雨轩 to the north-west, 杏花村 west of the 轩, 涧壑余清 south of the village, 镜水斋 behind the 轩 to the east, 抑斋 a north-west room, and 翠微堂 further west (S05 j81:1a; E1296). The editors add 得树亭, 吟籁亭, the gate 渊镜/屏岩 and 绿云酣 (E1303). Malone notes that the album shows rustic buildings, a well and vegetable plots, while the later plan S01 shows a pond instead of the plots and more buildings instead of the well (S02 p.80 n.32; E1301): the scene was rebuilt between 1744 and the plan's state. The shrine was named 春雨轩土地庙 in an archive file of 1858, when Xianfeng gave its two deities titles, tablets and a stele (S47; E1302).

Plan 样028-1 (NLC, ink, working sheet, 1831-1840; E1305). The record: first a vegetable plot 菜圃 under Kangxi; plaques 杏花春馆 and 杏花村 hung 1727; the 1744 leaf shows low huts, fences and apricots; in 1755 the front was rebuilt with the 春雨轩 hall, the 涧壑余清 gate and the 得树 pavilion; 1770 a rock peak behind 春雨轩; at the end of Qianlong 19 buildings of 71 bays were repainted, two of them of 楠木 (S310 rec. 8065). So the 1744 leaf is not the 1860 state here.

## Interior and setting

### Interior

Plaque 杏花春馆 in Yongzheng's hand; Qianlong's 1744 poem cut on a rock beside the lodge ("館旁峰石上刋御製杏花春館詩"); inside 春雨轩 the plaque 蕙气清阴, and on its rear porch the couplet "生機對物觀其妙 義府因心獲所寜"; plaques of 镜水斋, 抑斋, 翠微堂 in Qianlong's hand (S05 j81:1a; E1296). Tablets and a stele added to the earth shrine in 1858 (E1302).

### The garden around it

Apricot trees (文杏) all round the cottages, a vegetable plot and a well in 1744 (E1285, E1301); later a pond in place of the plots (E1301). A hill with a small city gate at the top and a hexagonal pavilion on its slope (E1308). On the album the gable walls of the earth shrine are painted red, against grey or white on other buildings (S47 pp.121-123; E0499).
